walkthroughs.body_html:
If God is omnipotent and omnibenevolent, why is there evil?

Christians distinguish moral evil (caused by humans) and natural evil (earthquakes, disease).

One response: humans have free will. Real love and goodness require choice, and choice means evil is possible. Adam and Eve's misuse of free will is called the Fall.

Christians believe Jesus will return and judge the living and the dead (Matthew 25 — sheep and goats).

Those who showed love — feeding the hungry, visiting prisoners — are welcomed; those who didn't are turned away.

The criteria are both faith in Jesus and a life that reflects God's love.

Heaven is eternal life with God. Many Christians see it as spiritual rather than literally streets of gold.

Hell is eternal separation from God. Some see it as literal fire, others as the absence of God's love.

Roman Catholics also believe in purgatory — a state of cleansing before entering heaven. Protestants generally reject this teaching.

mcqs.q: What do Christians mean by resurrection, and how does it differ from reincarnation?
options: Jesus was a human who became God after his resurrection.

Resurrection is the once-for-all bodily raising to eternal life at the end of time (modelled on Christ's resurrection); reincarnation is the soul's repeated rebirth into new bodies. They are distinct doctrines from different religious traditions.
Christians believe everyone is reincarnated until they accept Jesus.
Resurrection and reincarnation are basically the same idea of life after death.

mcqs.q: What is the doctrine of the Trinity?
options: Christians believe in three different gods.
The Trinity refers to heaven, earth and hell.
Christians believe everyone is reincarnated until they accept Jesus.
God is one being existing in three persons (Father, Son, Holy Spirit) — distinct in person but united in essence; Christians remain monotheistic.

mcqs.q: What do orthodox Christians believe about the nature of Jesus?
options: He is fully God and fully human at the same time (the incarnation) — both natures united in one person, as defined at the Council of Chalcedon.
Jesus was half God and half human.
The Trinity refers to heaven, earth and hell.
Jesus was a human who became God after his resurrection.
